newsitem.title: BELARUS: Ford opens car assembly plant in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Ford opens car assembly plant in Belarus.

text.p: Ford Motor Co, the world's second biggest automaker, opened an assembly plant in Belarus on Wednesday that can produce 6,000 vehicles a year.

The U.S. company has a 51 percent stake in the project to which it allocated $9.8 million out of the total $19.2 milllion investment. The Belarussian government has a 26 percent stake, while the rest belongs to the Belarussian Lada-OMC company.
The joint venture, named Ford Union, will assemble Escort cars and Transit vans in Obchak, just outside the capital Minsk.
Ford's Vice-Chairman Wayne Booker said that the Belarussian plant was its first but not the last project in the former Soviet Union. He gave no other details.

Last month, Belarus's parliament and President Alexander Lukashenko, who attended the opening ceremony and drove the first assembled car, gave the venture a five-year tax break and privileges on imports of parts for the cars.
Ford's venture is a rare western investment in Belarus, where market reforms have been almost halted.
